family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, collapse every run of one or more whitespace characters into a single space, and remove any leading or trailing whitespace from the result. Tabs and newlines count as whitespace just like regular spaces.
visible_tests: assert condense_whitespace('  leading and trailing  ') == 'leading and trailing'
hidden_tests: assert condense_whitespace('one  two   three    four') == 'one two three four'
assert condense_whitespace('   a   b   c   ') == 'a b c'
assert condense_whitespace('mix \t of \n whitespace') == 'mix of whitespace'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, remove characters that are identical to the immediately preceding character, so each maximal run of the same character collapses to a single occurrence. Non-adjacent duplicate characters elsewhere in the string are kept. An empty string returns an empty string.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return a copy of s with every character that is not an alphabetic letter removed, preserving the order and original case of the remaining letters.
reference:
def keep_only_letters(s):
    return "".join(c for c in s if c.isalpha())

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return a copy where the alphabetic letters are forced to alternate case, starting with uppercase for the first letter encountered, then lowercase for the second, and so on; only letters count toward the alternation, and non-letter characters are copied through unchanged at their original position.
hidden_tests: assert alternate_upper_lower('a b c d') == 'A b C d'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s and a list of integer indices, return a copy of s where the case of the character at each listed position is flipped (uppercase becomes lowercase and vice versa); characters at positions not listed, and non-alphabetic characters, are left unchanged. Indices outside the valid range of s are simply ignored.
hidden_tests: assert toggle_case_at_indices('longer string here', [0, 7, 14]) == 'Longer String Here'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s and a single delimiter character delim, return a copy of s where the first alphabetic character immediately following each occurrence of delim is converted to uppercase; all other characters keep their original case. The very first character of the string is unaffected unless it directly follows a delim character.
visible_tests: assert capitalize_after_delimiter('no delimiter here', '.') == 'no delimiter here'
hidden_tests: assert capitalize_after_delimiter('hello. world. there.', '.') == 'hello. World. There.'

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, considering only its alphabetic characters in order, return True if each letter alternates in case with the previous one (no two consecutive letters share the same case); non-letter characters are ignored and do not break the alternation. A string with fewer than two letters is always considered alternating.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s consisting only of digit characters, return True if every pair of adjacent digits alternates between odd and even parity (for example '1234' alternates odd, even, odd, even). Return True for a string with 0 or 1 digit.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given two strings a and b, interleave their characters one at a time starting with a: a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1], and so on. Once the shorter string runs out of characters, append the remaining tail of the longer string unchanged.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return a tuple of two strings: the first containing the characters of s found at even indices (0, 2, 4, ...) in order, and the second containing the characters found at odd indices (1, 3, 5, ...) in order.
reference:
def split_alternate_indices(s):
    return (s[0::2], s[1::2])

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, considering only its alphabetic characters in order and ignoring case, return True if the letters alternate between vowel and consonant (no two consecutive letters are both vowels or both consonants). Non-letter characters are ignored entirely. A string with fewer than two letters is always considered alternating.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s and a positive integer min_run, compress s by replacing every maximal run of identical consecutive characters whose length is at least min_run with that character followed by its run length as digits; runs shorter than min_run are left as their original, uncompressed characters. An empty string returns an empty string.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a list of (character, count) tuples, reconstruct and return the string formed by repeating each character the given number of times, concatenated in the order the tuples appear. A count of 0 contributes nothing to the result, and an empty list returns an empty string.
reference:
def decompress_counts(pairs):
    return "".join(ch * cnt for ch, cnt in pairs)

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return a list of (character, count) tuples describing the maximal runs of consecutive identical characters in s, in the order they occur. An empty string returns an empty list.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return the number of maximal runs of consecutive identical characters in s (for example 'aaabccc' has 3 runs). An empty string has 0 runs.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, return a tuple (character, length) describing the longest maximal run of a single repeated character in s. If two runs tie for longest, return the one that occurs first in the string. An empty string returns ('', 0).

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s and a string delims whose individual characters are all treated as delimiters, split s into a list of non-empty tokens breaking at any character found in delims. Consecutive delimiters, and leading or trailing delimiters, never produce empty tokens in the result.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a camelCase or PascalCase string s, split it into a list of its component words by breaking immediately before each uppercase letter (an uppercase letter always starts a new word). Each returned word keeps its original casing exactly as it appeared. An empty string returns an empty list.

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a snake_case string s, split it on underscore characters and return a list of the non-empty component words in order. Consecutive underscores, and leading or trailing underscores, do not produce empty strings in the result.
reference:
def tokenize_snake_case(s):
    return [part for part in s.split('_') if part]

family: string manipulation (case, reversal, counting characters, palindromes, anagrams)
spec: Given a string s, split it into a list of maximal runs of consecutive characters that are either all letters or all digits, preserving order. Any character that is neither a letter nor a digit acts only as a separator (it never appears in the output) and always forces a break, even between an adjacent letter run and digit run.
